commits.message:
A turned colour with no room for its rounding holds still, and the wheel's bounds are settled once (rich-effects-wps6)

Review (high) of #404: at truecolor a fill bounded by a lighter and a
darker ink snapped between its turn and its rest frame to frame, since
whether hueTurned's two 8-bit colours fit its bounds changed with the hue.
Bounds narrower than ROUNDING_GAP, the widest those two can part, now
hold the colour still at every t; at least that wide, one always fits.
A wheel jump test at truecolor fails without it.

matchOn goes back to the memoised table matches; the wheel's bounds are
memoised per Drawn and its indexed candidates measured once per theme and
depth. contrastStop gives the stop scale one home beside luminanceRatio,
sharing WCAG's flare. The docs' wheel paragraph says what the code keeps.

The wheel keeps every word pair at its floor, at truecolor and 256 (rich-effects-wps6)

The wheel turned hue at fixed OKLCH lightness and claimed that kept words
reading as they did. It does not: equal lightness is not equal luminance
across hues, so truecolor pairs drifted under their floor (50 of 60 seeded
pairs), and at 256 colours each turned slot was rounded to the cube without
its partner (the ticket's strip: 226 of 601 frames under 4.5:1).

A colour now turns at its own relative luminance, so contrast is kept by
construction, and is written as the colour nearest its turn whose luminance
stays within bounds derived from every word pair it is drawn in: each pair's
contrast to spare above its floor is split between its turning sides. One
written colour per segment per frame, so powerline caps still match their
cells. The resting colour is always a candidate and always within bounds.

ColorSpec.indexed lists the colours a depth writes by index; matchOn scores
that list, so the wheel's candidates and the writer's rounding are one set.

A loop on a sixteen-colour terminal holds every cell on its slot (rich-effects-759a) (#403)

* A loop on a sixteen-colour terminal holds every cell on its slot (rich-effects-759a)

At "ansi" every move a loop makes is a jump to another slot, and a strong
enough light carried a cell there: pulse spent about half its period on
white over a bright-black fill. onColors and wheel now draw through
stillOnSlots, which holds every cell still where the depth writes only the
sixteen slots. atShares is left moving, because ProgressBar's pulse flashes
a slot at 16 colours as Rich's does.

* Sixteen-colour hold: public docs say it, WINDOWS is checked, the prose stops contradicting itself (rich-effects-759a)

onColors' and wheel's JSDoc now say they hold still on a sixteen-colour
terminal; docs/effects.md and stillOnSlots' header no longer claim every
move is a jump, only one that shows; the hold-still suite also renders at
ColorDepth.WINDOWS, which fails when WINDOWS leaves onlySlots.
